children: Wall Street's major market averages advanced on Monday as investor attention turned to the upcoming U.S.-China summit.
The blue-chip Dow
was last +0.6%, the benchmark S&P 500 (
) was last +1.2%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite
) was last +1.8%.
Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:
AMD hits $1T valuation amid broader semiconductor rally:
Advanced Micro Devices
a $1 trillion market capitalization for the first time, rising over 9% to a record high of $611.57. The stock was among a broader rally in chip and AI companies, with Intel
up about 12% at $120.96 and Micron
gaining about 3%, while Nvidia
rose about 1.4%. AMD is the fourth U.S. chipmaker to surpass a trillion dollar market valuation, following Nvidia, Broadcom
, and Micron. The broader technology rally comes as oil prices fell and Treasury yields eased, with the 10-year Treasury yield falling to 4.96% from 5.01% on Friday.
Major news outlets sue Trump over White House press credential ban:
CNN
, MS NOW
, and Politico

a joint First Amendment lawsuit against President Donald Trump after being barred from White House access. "We are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," the outlets said in a joint statement. The lawsuit argues the credential revocation violates constitutional protections, stating that "this ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles."
Crude oil drops as U.S. weighs diplomacy in Middle East:
Crude oil futures  fell for a fourth straight session after President Trump reportedly decided against bombing Yemen and indicated he was open to diplomacy with Iran. Front-month Nymex crude
for October delivery tumbled 4.9% to $95.36/bbl, and front-month Brent crude
for November delivery slipped 3.9% to $99.85/bbl. Five of the day's 10 largest losers on the S&P 500 are in the oil and gas sector, including ConocoPhillips
down 3%, Occidental Petroleum
down 2.6%, and ExxonMobil
down 2.4%.
Tesla bench trial begins over California racial discrimination suit:
Tesla

shares rose about 4% as a bench trial began in Oakland over California Civil Rights Department allegations of widespread racial harassment and pay disparity at its Fremont assembly plant. The lawsuit, filed in 2022, alleges workers encountered racial slurs and graffiti and that Tesla failed to adequately address the conduct. California law does not place a cap on damages for workplace discrimination, meaning Tesla could face damages totaling millions of dollars if found liable. Tesla has denied wrongdoing and said it does not tolerate discrimination.
